brief: Cross-asset correlations are strengthening as macro catalysts accumulate: this Friday's nonfarm payrolls, Middle East flare-ups, and a global rates tantrum, arriving as the market clears second-quarter earnings and enters a thin stretch for micro catalysts. The note argues this combination leaves investors underhedged and expecting choppiness in the weeks ahead, even though hedges remain remarkably light across most major markets. As support, it notes equity volatility is only modestly cheap relative to single-stock volatility, with the VIX underperforming the VIXEQ index at a -0.5 z-score on a one-year lookback, while the MOVE index, a bond-market volatility gauge, sits at a 0.2 z-score and a seasonal low. Because oil and rates are now driving macro price action and their effects propagate across markets, the note concludes the simplest hedge is the best one. It likens current pricing to an insurance market still willing to write cheap property-and-casualty protection despite storm clouds already overhead, arguing investors do not need to identify which specific risk breaks first before buying that protection now.
